prisoner.name: Ilse Asplund
prisoner.description: Ilse Asplund is an Arizona environmental activist and community health educator prosecuted with the Arizona Five. She entered prison in October 1991 following a negotiated resolution of the federal case.

cases.charges: Reduced federal charge in Arizona Five prosecution — individual statutory count unverified
cases.sentence: Sentenced September 19, 1991; began custody October 3. Contemporary reporting describes thirty days to serve and a suspended balance, followed by house detention and probation. The exact release day and statutory plea count remain unverified; the suspended balance and home detention are not counted as jail time.

case_research.custody_evidence: Contemporary prison-entry report and later history establish actual custody and subsequent release.

prisoner.name: Erik Bowers Ryberg
prisoner.description: Erik Ryberg participated in the Cove–Mallard forest-defense campaign in Idaho. He was jailed after obstructing a Forest Service vehicle at the protest camp, and his conviction was affirmed on appeal.

cases.charges: Interference with Forest Service officers — 36 CFR 261.3(a) and (c)
cases.sentence: Six months with four suspended; contemporary reporting and a later letter confirm sixty days served. Sentenced in February 1994 and held in Moscow, Idaho. The Ninth Circuit affirmed the conviction January 6, 1995. Exact custody endpoints remain unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: Contemporary report describes him serving the term; August1994 letter reports the completed sixty days.

entries.custody_evidence: Contemporary report describes him serving the term; August1994 letter reports the completed sixty days.

prisoner.name: Jennifer Prichard
prisoner.description: Jennifer Prichard was jailed during the Cove–Mallard logging-road campaign in Idaho. After earlier custody, she returned to jail in 1994 for refusing court-ordered restitution to the road-building contractor. The two periods belong to the same original sentence.

cases.charges: Cove–Mallard road-blockade conviction — individual count unverified
cases.sentence: The coalition report states that she served the initial thirty-one days of a ninety-day sentence during summer and fall 1993. Individual custody intervals within that year are not resolved. This is the earlier portion, not an additional ninety-day term.

cases.charges: Probation violation for refusal to pay restitution following Cove–Mallard blockade
cases.sentence: Returned to custody July 12, 1994 to serve the remaining fifty-nine days of the original ninety-day sentence. A contemporaneous statement places her in Idaho County Jail, Grangeville. Exact release remains unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: The later coalition account expressly documents thirty-one days already served in1993.
Named return-to-custody date and August prisoner statement establish sustained confinement.

entries.custody_evidence: The later coalition account expressly documents thirty-one days already served in1993. Named return-to-custody date and August prisoner statement establish sustained confinement.

prisoner.name: Peggy Sue McRae
prisoner.description: Peggy Sue McRae participated in the Cove–Mallard forest-defense campaign. She was jailed in Idaho in 1994 after refusing to pay restitution to the contractor building the logging road.

cases.charges: Refusal to pay court-ordered restitution following Cove–Mallard road-blockade case
cases.sentence: Committed July 7, 1994 for sixty-one days after refusing restitution. The coalition published her statement from Idaho County Jail in August. The exact underlying plea count, any earlier custody episode and the release date remain unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: Her published statement from jail and the dated commitment report establish multi-day custody.

prisoner.name: Panagioti Tsolkas
prisoner.description: Panagioti Tsolkas is an environmental organizer associated with Everglades Earth First! and the Palm Beach County Environmental Coalition. His accounts document jail time during the 1999 WTO protests and following a Florida power-plant blockade.

cases.charges: Detention during Seattle WTO protests — released without criminal charges
cases.sentence: His November 2009 retrospective letter states that he spent five days in Seattle jail during the 1999 WTO protests before release without criminal charges. Individual arrest and release days remain unverified.

cases.charges: Unlawful assembly, trespassing and resisting an officer without violence
cases.sentence: Sentenced and jailed February 2, 2009 following the February 2008 power-plant protest. His February 19 update records thirteen days actually served before release on appellate bond, against a sixty-day sentence. Later appeal outcome remains unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: Named first-person retrospective expressly reports five days in Seattle jail.
First-person post-release update establishes thirteen days served; radio report anchors commitment.

entries.custody_evidence: Named first-person retrospective expressly reports five days in Seattle jail. First-person post-release update establishes thirteen days served; radio report anchors commitment.

Personal/support website not established; organizational sources remain citations only.

prisoner.name: Lynne Purvis
prisoner.description: Lynne Purvis is an environmental activist jailed after an Everglades-area power-plant blockade. Following release, she spoke about the protest, her trial and conditions in Palm Beach County custody.

cases.charges: Unlawful assembly, trespassing and resisting an officer without violence
cases.sentence: Sentenced and jailed February 2, 2009 for thirty days after the February 2008 blockade. A co-defendant reported her continued confinement; a March interview confirms release. The prospective February 24 release estimate is not entered as an actual release date.

case_research.custody_evidence: Contemporaneous prison letter describes her continued custody, followed by an actual post-release interview.

prisoner.name: Willow Cordes-Eklund
prisoner.description: Willow Cordes-Eklund participated in a Maine protest against construction of industrial wind turbines in mountain habitat. She was convicted of failing to disperse and jailed in August 2011.

cases.charges: Failure to disperse — Kibby wind-project blockade
cases.sentence: Sentenced June 21, 2011 to ten days; reporting was stayed until August 25. An August 29 movement notice confirms she was then in Somerset County Jail and that the term began August 25. The earlier sentencing report named Franklin County; the custody notice identifies her actual location. Release day remains unverified.

prisoner.name: Erik Gillard
prisoner.description: Erik Gillard participated in the 2010 Kibby wind-project protest in Maine. He was convicted of failing to disperse and entered jail following sentencing in June 2011.

cases.charges: Failure to disperse — Kibby wind-project blockade
cases.sentence: Sentenced June 21, 2011 to ten days in jail and a fine. The contemporary hearing report states that he began serving immediately after the hearing. Actual commitment is verified; the exact release date and completion of the entire term remain unverified.

prisoner.name: Stevie Lynn Lowe
prisoner.description: Stevie Lynn Lowe joined the Barley Barber Swamp protest in Florida. A jury acquitted her of trespassing but convicted her of resisting arrest without violence, resulting in jail time before release on appellate bond.

cases.charges: Resisting arrest without violence — Barley Barber Swamp protest; acquitted of trespass
cases.sentence: Sentenced July 23, 2009 to ninety days and probation. She remained in custody during the July 27 appellate-bond proceedings; a later movement report confirms bond release. The ninety-day sentence is not recorded as time actually served. Exact release and final appeal outcome remain unverified.
